github.owner: Python leaves owner/repo nullable because GitHubVFS also takes them as constructor arguments and raises when neither supplied them; TypeScript has no such escape hatch, so requiring them in the schema is its honest contract. A YAML mount naming neither is refused by both, at different moments.

qdrant.embed: TypeScript's client-side embedding seam, a callable no YAML block can carry: the JS qdrant client has no fastembed, so a caller vectorizes the search query in-process. Python embeds locally through qdrant-client[fastembed] and switches to the server with `cloud_inference`.

s3.httpAgentProvider: A caller-supplied HTTP agent factory, a callable no YAML block can carry; python's aiohttp session pool is configured through the accessor.
s3.presignedUrlProvider: The browser's authentication model: a signer callable in place of credentials. Python has no browser runtime.

language_only_vfs_names.opfs: Browser-only OPFS backend. Python has no browser runtime, so there is nothing to mirror.

lancedb.caches_reads: Both languages compute it per mount from the URI scheme (remote tables cache, local ones do not): lancedb.py sets it in __init__, lancedb.ts in its constructor. The generators disagree because python reads the class attribute, which is still the base default at class level, while the TypeScript walk reads the constructor assignment. A per-instance value, not a table, so there is nothing to single-source.

browser.history: See python: the history view mount is workspace-internal.

node.history: See python: the history view mount is workspace-internal.

python.history: The /.bash_history view mount is created by the workspace itself and is never named in YAML or a snapshot, so it registers commands without a build_vfs entry.
